against.text: Nothing independent supports the Dulce insider: John Greenewald found no evidence Castello existed, the photograph circulated as his evidence of bodies is a frame from the 2000 film The 6th Day, and Norio Hayakawa, who has worked the question since 1988, concludes the base does not seem to exist.

The TR-3B's own specification fails: the 1998 transcript gives the craft as 600 feet across on one slide and 300 on the next, and, on the board's reading of its slide 72, calls mercury at 150 kelvin a plasma, while NIST gives mercury's melting point as 234.31 K. The aerospace historian Peter Merlin says no Steve Stenson, whom Fouche named as site manager, ever commanded AFFTC.

Lazar's credentials do not check out: Glenn Campbell found no Lazar in any MIT student directory from 1978 to 1990, as Tom Mahood records, and Caltech says it has never had a graduate degree in electronics; the Los Alamos directory page carrying his name covers DOE employees and an outside contractor, and Mahood concludes he was an electronic technician for Kirk-Mayer.

Corso's sworn 1998 affidavit says he was a member of Eisenhower's National Security Council, while his own service record lists him on the Operations Coordinating Board, which reported to the Council and was not the Council; the 322 pages of his FBI file contain no occurrence of UFO, flying saucer, Roswell or extraterrestrial.

The committee's own letters on the missing scientists frame their subject as unconfirmed public reporting and footnote every factual assertion to newspapers; the letters say at least ten people from 2023, while Fox News reported eleven since 2022.

The Kirtland admissions are themselves weak ground: Doty's reported admission is paraphrased throughout and never quotes him, and he has since called the story that he drove Bennewitz mad false in every aspect; on the board's reading his statements establish only what he said.

answer.text: Tal Levesque, who wrote as Jason Bishop III, told Adam Gorightly by email in November 2015 that Thomas Castello was a creation, a myth, and described sending a hundred large packets of material to authors and lecturers, who mixed it into their talks, articles and books; on the board's reading the later Dulce sources agree because one person supplied them by one method.

Bob Lazar's account of nine discs at S-4 reached the public through George Knapp's KLAS-TV series and his own 1991 videotape; the credential checks and the properties of the real element 115 cut against it, and Stanton Friedman, a UFO proponent, found no diplomas, transcripts or yearbook pages.

Claims drift when retold: the board records that the widely repeated claim that AARO acknowledged Yankee Blue in Volume I does not survive a full-text check, that promotional language saying Michael Herrera is testifying to Congress is unsupported, and that the CIA names Lockheed only as one member of a four-company consortium where a retelling had the Glomar Explorer leased to Lockheed Martin for twenty years.

Some of the confusion was deliberate. William Moore stated in 1989 that he had cooperated with Air Force counterintelligence and knowingly passed false information to Paul Bennewitz, and Richard Doty has said he was tasked with hoaxing documents and feeding false information to UFO researchers including Bennewitz.

c-639862f702.text: Stated inference, and it is a short one. 150 K is 84 K below mercury's melting point of 234.31 K at one atmosphere. Mercury's melting curve has a positive slope, so a pressure of 250,000 atmospheres raises the melting point rather than lowering it, putting the material further into the solid region and not closer to a gas. A plasma is an ionised gas. The specification therefore describes a solid and calls it a plasma, and it does so before any question of superconductivity, rotation or gravity is reached.

c-d2096f9588.text: THE COLLISION, STATED WITHOUT OVERSTATEMENT AND WITHOUT SOFTENING. Nothing about moscovium is stable, machinable, storable or available in gram quantities: it is produced one atom at a time at cross sections of about one picobarn and its decay chains run to completion within seconds. for.text: The popular story is right that secrecy was managed by deception: the CIA historian Gerald Haines wrote that Air Force investigators knowingly gave false explanations to protect U-2 and OXCART flights, and the Robertson Panel recommended debunking through the mass media and watching civilian UFO groups.

The Wall Street Journal reported in June 2025 that Air Force personnel were briefed into a fictitious reverse-engineering programme called Yankee Blue, shown flying-saucer photographs and bound by NDAs, and that the practice convinced hundreds of people. It is press reporting; the memo it described has not been released, and Volume I does not mention the programme.

The Roswell story is right that the 1947 public account was false: the Air Force's 1994 report acknowledged that the weather balloon explanation had been a cover story, and GAO found the base's messages for the period destroyed with no disposition authority.

Some figures at the centre of the stories are real: Philip Corso's service record shows him briefly chief of a Foreign Technology Division in the Army's research and development office in 1962, and Edgar Fouche was a real Air Force avionics sergeant whose own compilation records temporary duty to the Nellis range in 1979; on the board's reading his papers document an ordinary career and are silent on the aerospace claims.

House Oversight's chairman and Rep. Burlison did write in April 2026 to NASA, the FBI, the Department of War and the Department of Energy about reported deaths and disappearances of at least ten people, after the February 2026 disappearance of William McCasland, which Fox News reports prompted the probe.

lead.text: The popular story runs furthest ahead of the record where a single source seeded many retellings: the Dulce base's central insider was confessed in 2015 as an invention by the man who says he mailed a hundred packets to make the story look independently sourced, and the TR-3B first appears in one 1998 presentation given, in its own words, about a new book that the Library of Congress catalogues as science fiction. Some of the confusion was manufactured: two participants have said they fed a civilian false UFO information at Kirtland.

open: Which of the many sources that repeat the Dulce story can be traced to Levesque's hundred packets, and which, if any, arose independently?
Does the spring 2023 memo ordering Yankee Blue stopped exist, and what will the remanded FOIA search find?
How or whether does the TR-3B appear in the book Fouche's transcript was written to promote, whose text has not been opened?
Did NASA, the FBI, the Department of War or the Department of Energy answer the letters by the 27 April 2026 deadline, and what did they say?
What did the Bennewitz operation protect, if it was protecting anything, and why has no official report acknowledged it?

threads.text: The scientists thread shows how a written assertion becomes a storyline. In January 2016 Tom DeLonge wrote to John Podesta that when Roswell crashed they shipped it to the laboratory at Wright-Patterson, which records what DeLonge asserted in writing, not what happened; the general on that thread had commanded the Air Force Research Laboratory there, and press reporting ties the committee's April 2026 probe of deaths and disappearances to his disappearance in February 2026. The probe is run by the same committee and member as the UAP inquiry, which the board records as a structural link, not a finding.
